period-georgian-townhouse.description: A three-bay brick townhouse of about 1760: rubbed-brick flat arches, six-over-six sashes, a fanlight over a panelled door, and a parapet hiding the slate roof.

period-georgian-terrace.label: Georgian terrace range
period-georgian-terrace.description: A five-bay run of yellow London stock brick with a basement area behind iron railings, the piano nobile marked by taller first-floor sashes.

period-georgian-stone-house.label: Ashlar town house
period-georgian-stone-house.description: Palladian manners in dressed limestone: rusticated ground floor, quoined corners and a pedimented doorcase, as in Bath or Dublin.

period-regency-terrace.label: Regency stucco terrace
period-regency-terrace.description: Painted stucco of the 1820s with a continuous iron balcony under a tented canopy at first-floor level, low hipped slate roof and deep eaves.

period-georgian-shop.label: Georgian bow-window shop
period-georgian-shop.description: A two-story shop-house with a many-paned bow window beside the door and a hanging trade sign, typical of a market town high street.

period-federal-house.label: Federal clapboard house
period-federal-house.description: White-painted clapboard with green shutters, paired end chimneys and an elliptical fanlight, the New England house of about 1800.

period-greek-revival.label: Greek Revival house
period-greek-revival.description: Gable-end to the street with a full pediment and a columned porch: the temple-front house of the 1830s and 1840s.

period-brownstone.label: Brownstone row house
period-brownstone.description: A high-stoop brownstone of the 1870s: raised basement, tall parlour-floor windows under stone hoods and a heavy bracketed cornice.

period-brownstone-pair.label: Brownstone double house
period-brownstone-pair.description: A wider brownstone with round-headed windows, on the Italianate pattern of Brooklyn and Harlem.

period-italianate-row.label: Italianate row house
period-italianate-row.description: A bracketed cornice, arched upper windows and a projecting ground-floor bay, painted ochre: the mid-century Italianate row house.

period-mansard-house.label: Second Empire house
period-mansard-house.description: A slate mansard with dormers and iron cresting over a brick body: the fashionable house of the 1860s and 1870s.

period-victorian-shop.label: Victorian shop with fascia
period-victorian-shop.description: Plate glass under a lettered fascia and a striped blind, with lodgings above. The standard high-street shop from the 1850s onward.

period-victorian-grocer.label: Corner grocer
period-victorian-grocer.description: A two-story grocer's with produce crates on the pavement and a painted fascia; the shop the neighbourhood buys its bread from.

period-cast-iron-warehouse.label: Cast-iron warehouse
period-cast-iron-warehouse.description: Rows of arched windows between slender painted iron columns, as in SoHo or Glasgow's warehouse streets of the 1860s.

period-tenement-storefront.label: Tenement with storefront
period-tenement-storefront.description: A five-story brick walk-up with a shop at street level, an iron fire escape zigzagging down the front and a water tank on the roof.

period-tenement-walkup.label: Tenement walk-up
period-tenement-walkup.description: The dumbbell tenement's street face: three bays, a double door under a transom, fire escape, and a corbelled brick cornice.

period-chinese-shophouse.label: Chinese shophouse
period-chinese-shophouse.description: Grey brick and a grey tile roof with raised ridge ends; folding timber shutters open the whole ground floor to the street, lanterns at the eave.
period-chinese-shophouse.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon

period-chinese-courtyard-gate.label: Courtyard house gate range
period-chinese-courtyard-gate.description: The street range of a siheyuan: a studded vermilion gate with drum stones, flanked by lattice windows under a tiled roof.
period-chinese-courtyard-gate.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon

period-machiya.label: Machiya townhouse
period-machiya.description: A Kyoto-style merchant house: fine koshi lattice and an indigo noren at street level, plastered upper wall with a slit window, dark kawara tiles.
period-machiya.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon

period-machiya-shop.label: Edo merchant shop
period-machiya-shop.description: A wider shop with paper-screened upper windows and a vertical signboard, the kind that lined a post-town's main street.
period-machiya-shop.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon

period-hanok.label: Hanok house
period-hanok.description: Dark posts framing white plaster panels and paper-screened windows, a raised wooden floor, and a heavy grey giwa roof whose eaves lift at the corners.
period-hanok.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon

period-giyofu-house.label: Meiji Western-style house

period-giyofu-house.periodGroup: East Asia · Qing, Edo and Joseon
